researched_by: the council's own traffic order consultation pages and order documents, the 2012 consolidated off-street parking order, council news releases, contemporary BBC/Cambrian News/CaravanTimes reporting and a motorhome-press account of the 2020 stopover trial
policy_summary:
Ceredigion is the Welsh authority that tried the aire idea before Gwynedd did, dropped it, and has been tightening ever since. There is currently NO designated overnight motorhome provision anywhere in the county.

The restriction is the oldest continuous one in Wales. After roughly 20 vans colonised the south promenade in summer 2013 - some for six weeks - the council consulted in 2014, made an experimental order in spring 2015 banning caravans and campervans from waiting 11pm-8am on New Promenade and South Marine Terrace, and made it permanent in December 2017 after 26 objections (mostly from outside the county) were overridden. It has just been extended: Aberystwyth Seafront Amendment Order No. 13, consulted on to 27 December 2024 and made with effect from 30 March 2026, adds a 'Prohibition of Waiting for Caravans and Motor Caravans 11pm-8am' on the landward side of King Street and on two further sections of New Promenade, alongside new 8am-8pm pay-and-display with a four-hour maximum. Prom charging started 18 May 2026.

Off-street, the position is that you may PARK overnight but may not SLEEP. Long-stay car parks sell a 24-hour ticket at GBP5-7 and charging runs only 08:00-18:00, so a van left in a bay overnight is legally parked; but article 9(e) of the consolidated off-street parking order prohibits using a parking place 'for sleeping or camping purposes' without the council's written authority, on pain of prosecution rather than a PCN. Park4night reports for the Aberystwyth seafront car park describe heavy 'sleeping and cooking in vehicles not permitted' signage, three or four designated motorhome/caravan day bays, and an enforcement officer threatening tickets for vans outside them.

The one moment of provision was a 2020 trial - written authority under that same clause - allowing caravanettes to sleep overnight at New Promenade car park in Aberystwyth and Quay Street car park in Cardigan. It ended on 30 September 2020, both car parks 'reverted to their normal regulations - no overnight sleeping', a promised 2021 review never produced a published outcome, and nothing has replaced it.

On the Welsh aires question: neither the Arosfan brand nor any equivalent scheme, trial or partnership appears anywhere in Ceredigion. Gwynedd opened its first Arosfan in 2023-24 and Anglesey copied it in autumn 2025; Ceredigion, whose own experiment predates both, has not gone back to the idea.
notes:
The trajectory is the exact inverse of South Ayrshire and of neighbouring Gwynedd. Ceredigion got to provision first, in the COVID summer of 2020 when campsites were shut and Councillor Endaf Edwards was counting 29 to 50 vans in Aberystwyth against four caravan bays, with chemical waste going into public toilets and road drains and the Blue Flag at risk. It opened two car parks, closed them after six weeks, and every subsequent decision has been restrictive.

The 2025-26 round is instructive because motorhomes are not the target and are collateral anyway. The Off-Street Parking Places Order 2025 (made 09/04/2025, operative 07/05/2025, revoking the 2012, 2014 and 2017 orders) is a revenue and turnover exercise - but it explicitly excludes motorhomes and campervans from the new long-stay season tickets, so the one cheap way to hold a bay for a week is closed to vans. The seafront amendment then removes the free 11pm-8am kerb. Turnover, not tourism, is the stated aim: the council wants prom spaces cycling every four hours to 'help boost trade'.

Worth being clear about the enforcement split. On-street 11pm-8am is a civil parking contravention with a PCN. Sleeping in an off-street car park is an offence under the parking places order carrying prosecution, not a penalty charge - which is why the signage says 'not permitted' rather than quoting a fine, and why enforcement in practice is a patrolling officer rather than a camera.

Mwnt is National Trust and Llangrannog beach parking is largely village/private; the council's estate on that stretch of coast is thin, so the practical rules south of Aberaeron are set by landowners rather than by Ceredigion.
open_questions: Does the Off-Street Parking Places Order 2025 carry forward article 9(e) of the 2012 consolidation ('no sleeping or camping')? The 2025 order PDF is too large to retrieve and the public notice and cabinet report do not mention it. The prohibition is assumed to survive because the notice says the revoked orders' provisions were 'reintroduced with modifications' and the signage on the ground still says so.

Which car parks the 2025 order admits caravanettes to, and at what tariff. The 2012 order allowed them at New Promenade (Aberystwyth), Church Road and Rock Street (New Quay) and Bath House, Mwldan, Fairfield and Quay Street (Cardigan) for a daily caravanette fee of about GBP6; the current fees page lists no caravan or caravanette class at all.

The exact extent of New Promenade car park, Aberystwyth - the street runs round the castle point and its postcode (SY23 2BQ) was terminated in 2022, so the pin is approximate and may sit on the wrong side of the bandstand.
Whether the 2021 review of the 2020 stopover trial ever happened, and what it concluded. No published outcome was found.

Whether the council's summer 2020 promise of 'additional measures' beyond signage produced anything at New Quay, Borth, Llangrannog or Tresaith. No coastal car park order or PSPO naming motorhomes was found outside Aberystwyth.
The exact street sections in Amendment Order No. 13 - the site notice gives locations 27, 28 and 29 by number and the maps are in a separate PDF that was not retrieved.

sites.notes: One of the two car parks where Ceredigion permitted overnight sleeping in caravanettes during the summer of 2020 - written authority under the clause that otherwise prohibits it. The trial ended on 30 September 2020 and the car park 'reverted to normal regulations - no overnight sleeping'. A 2021 review was promised and never published. Park4night reports for the adjoining seafront parking at South Marine Terrace (52.4115, -4.0889) describe current signage reading 'sleeping and cooking in vehicles not permitted', three or four designated motorhome/caravan day bays, and an enforcement officer threatening a ticket for using an undesignated bay. Pin is approximate: New Promenade curves round the castle point and its postcode was terminated in 2022.

sites.name: Quay Street Car Park, Cardigan
sites.notes: The other 2020 stopover trial car park. Caravanettes - vehicles constructed or adapted for sleeping in - could stay overnight provided they paid, stayed within marked bays and caused no obstruction. Reverted to no overnight sleeping on 30 September 2020. Still a Ceredigion long-stay car park with a 24-hour ticket, so parking overnight remains lawful; sleeping does not.

sites.name: New Promenade, South Marine Terrace, King Street and adjoining seafront streets, Aberystwyth
sites.notes: The oldest continuously enforced motorhome parking ban in Wales. Experimental order April 2015 covering New Promenade and South Marine Terrace after roughly 20 vans occupied the south prom in 2013, some for six weeks; made permanent December 2017 over 26 objections, most from outside Ceredigion. Extended by Aberystwyth Seafront Amendment Order No. 13 - consulted to 27 December 2024, made effective 30 March 2026 - which adds 'Prohibition of Waiting for Caravans and Motor Caravans 11pm-8am' on the landward side of King Street and on two further sections of New Promenade (a 55m stretch from the Pier Street junction and a further 90m). The same order brings 8am-8pm pay-and-display with a four-hour maximum to the seafront from 18 May 2026. The order is drafted as a prohibition of WAITING by vehicle class, so it bites whether or not anyone is asleep inside.

sites.notes: Article 9(e) of the Ceredigion County Council (Off-Street Parking Places) (Consolidation) Order 2012 prohibits using a parking place 'for sleeping or camping purposes' without the council's written authority, with liability to prosecution. The 2012 order was revoked by the Off-Street Parking Places Order 2025 (made 09/04/2025, operative 07/05/2025), whose public notice says the revoked provisions were reintroduced with modifications; the clause is assumed to survive but the order text could not be retrieved, hence medium confidence. Parking overnight is a different matter and is lawful - long stay car parks sell a 24-hour ticket at GBP5-7 and charging hours are only 08:00-18:00. Motorhomes and campervans are expressly excluded from the long-stay season tickets introduced in 2025.
